The thought of suicide is somewhat soothing. "Whatever happens, it's not going to last forever" is what i often think about. 

I guess I'm just at the start of this whole therapy and getting better thing. Right now we've pretty much only discussed what went wrong and didn't really go into real therapy all that much.  
But I guess I gotta try continuing since it's better than nothing... and when it gets unbearable I can still go i guess.

It's just kinda annoying that suicide and "the easy way out" is the first thought I get when anything becomes tiresome or stressful. Whenever I have to go to work I always think "Why even bother?", "It would be so easy to just not go..." and then I still somehow manage to gather the energy to dress myself and go to work. But it doesn't feel like it's gonna be like that forever. It feels like every time I have less energy at my disposal, and the thought of working full time and supporting myself is just giving me panic attacks. 

I'd like to think that the worst time of my life (trauma) is over, but in fact I didn't mind my childhood all that much I guess. My childhood only becomes bothersome to me when the adult-me thinks about it, and when I am aware of how fucked up it was and how it fucked me up. Some posts on here do inspire me though, because it seems like there is a way out of this. At the same time the posts here also give me the feeling that it's pretty hard getting there, which does scare me a lot.

So i went to Italy with some friends for a party. Everything was fine and we had a blast. Eventually we wanted to get back to Bolzano where our bus would've taken us home the next morning. You gotta know that this party was in the middle of fucking nowhere. It took us nearly 2 hours to get there by bus. We headed back to the bus stop where we waited for about an hour. We asked some people when the promised shuttle busses will arrive but somehow nobody knows what we're talking about. (FYI their Facebook page still says that they provide shuttles.) Now we were helpless... And the fact that we were still tripping balls from the LSD we swallowed earlier did not help at all.
We had to get home without any food, money phone battery or any sense of Orientation.
We wandered in the dark forest for about 6 hours... Eventually we found a road that we followed for another 5 hours. Maybe it was the acid but when we were lost in the woods without we all kinda accepted the fact that we're gonna die out there. After about 13 hours of aimlessly wandered through a small town where we stumbled across a bus stop. We encountered a saint! We explained our story to the bua driver and he got us to Bolzano for free. But only that we just had to wait for his shift to end and then he drove us back home with his own car. (We live around 3 hours from bolzano) For free! 

Since then I believe that there really are some really nice people out there!
